dossier.public_summary: The dip is not steady across sectors and the four predicted transits are inconsistent in depth, with the fourth sector showing no dip at all and all detections falling in one observing gap. Combined with many nearby stars that could mimic the dip and an inconclusive centroid, the signal is best explained by a few variable or contamination events rather than a single transiting planet.

reasons.why: Depth changes by a factor of ~36 and p_constant is significant (sector_depths_by_source verdict changes_within_a_source); a planet should have steady depth within one source, not vanish in sector 103.
Individual transit depths are inconsistent; the signal is driven by two deep dips in sectors 66 and 93 while the fourth event is undetected, so not a repeated transit.
reasons.value: 1.51e-18, chi2 86.09 dof 3, one transit 207 ppm sigma -7.0

reasons.why: All detected events cluster in two sectors and coincide with a single gap, unlikely for a periodic planet and typical of a few bad/variable events.

Many faint stars can produce the 4535 ppm dip with a <11% eclipse; high contamination plus inconclusive centroid (centroid_all verdict inconclusive) leaves a blended/variable neighbour as the best explanation against a faint, variable 3585 K star.
